metadata.title: Security Assessment Results - Secure Identity Provider (Microsoft Entra ID)

findings.title: Persistent Session Support Undermines Continuous Identity Assurance
findings.description: Microsoft Entra ID currently allows persistent session mechanisms (e.g., 'Keep Me Signed In'), enabling long-lived authentication sessions that can bypass continuous identity assurance requirements. This reduces resistance to session hijacking, shared-device exposure, and post-authentication misuse.

associated-risk.title: Loss of Continuous Authentication Assurance
associated-risk.description: Persistent sessions weaken identity assurance by extending trust beyond the moment of authentication without sufficient revalidation.

findings.title: Upstream Federation Dependencies Affect End-to-End Identity Assurance
findings.description: Primary user authentication in Entra ID depends on upstream on-premises federation services (ADFS and Shibboleth). Assurance of identity claims is therefore dependent on the security, availability, and configuration of external identity providers and secure token exchange mechanisms.

associated-risk.title: Extended Trust Chain and Downgrade Risk
associated-risk.description: Federation increases the length of the identity trust chain and can introduce downgrade or resilience risks if upstream identity providers do not maintain equivalent assurance guarantees.

remediations.title: Disable Persistent Session Features
remediations.description: Remove or strictly constrain persistent session mechanisms to ensure continuous identity assurance and session revalidation.

tasks.title: Disable Keep Me Signed In
tasks.description: Update Entra ID authentication and session policies to prevent long-lived persistent sessions.

remediations.title: Reduce Federation Dependency and Strengthen Assurance
remediations.description: Strengthen or reduce reliance on upstream federation by improving native identity assurance capabilities.

tasks.title: Migrate to Native Entra ID Assurance Mechanisms
tasks.description: Transition from custom federation overlays and MFA integrations to Entra ID native External Authentication Methods (EAM) and identity protection controls.
